facts.text: PEI's bioscience cluster reported private sector company revenues of more than $612 million, growing 84 percent since 2018, making bioscience the province's second-largest industry by GDP impact.
The PEI bioscience sector employs 2,200 people with an average annual salary of $79,300, making the cluster the highest-paying private sector employer in the province.
Sekisui Diagnostics is expanding its P.E.I. facility and hiring 25 new staff with $3.9 million in support from the province.
Port Charlottetown expects to welcome more than 131,000 cruise passengers and 57,800 crew in 2025, including six inaugural calls and two overnight stays.
The University of Prince Edward Island boosts the provincial GDP by over $228 million, according to its economic impact report.

overview: Charlottetown grew 7.5 percent between 2016 and 2021, from 36,094 to 38,809 residents, and its 17,184 occupied dwellings sit within a compact 44.27 square kilometres. As the provincial capital it combines government, health care and university employment with a fast-growing bioscience cluster and a busy summer cruise and tourism season.

For a local business, that means a small but dense and growing market where most customers live minutes from downtown, plus a seasonal wave of visitors. Being visible to both residents and tourists, and to the well-paid bioscience workforce, shapes how a business should present itself.

byService.lead-generation: Lead generation in Charlottetown should run two tracks, one for the 17,184 resident households and one timed to the cruise and tourist season, when demand for services spikes.
byService.seo: Charlottetown SEO benefits from a city of only 44.27 square kilometres, since a single strong local profile can cover every neighbourhood, but it must also capture visitor searches for the island.
byService.website-development: A Charlottetown website should load fast on mobile for visitors arriving by ship or car, and serve the residents who joined the city during its 7.5 percent growth to 2021.
byService.branding: Branding in Charlottetown can pair island charm with the professionalism expected by government, university and bioscience customers, giving a business a distinct place in a small market.
